ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is the power supply E, and above it a resistor R1 is first connected in series; after passing through R1, the right side of the circuit forms a parallel part between the upper and lower end nodes, in which there is a fixed-resistor branch and a sliding rheostat branch labeled R2. The slider of R2 is connected to the upper end node through the wire on the right side, and the lower end of R2 is connected to the bottom node. Then reason: because the slider of R2 is connected to the upper end node, what is actually connected into the circuit is that section of resistance wire from the slider to the lower end of R2. When the slider moves upward, the length of the resistance wire from the slider to the lower end becomes longer, so the effective resistance of R2 connected into the circuit increases. Under the voltage condition across the two ends of this parallel branch, if the branch resistance becomes larger, then the current through this sliding rheostat branch becomes smaller. Therefore, the current in the sliding rheostat decreases.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image: battery E, a series resistor R1, then a parallel network including the sliding resistor R2 whose wiper is tied to the upper node. Determine which part of R2 is actually in circuit: the segment from the wiper down to the bottom terminal. When the slider moves upward, that segment becomes longer, so the effective resistance of the sliding resistor increases. Apply Ohm’s law/branch-current reasoning: larger branch resistance gives a smaller current through that sliding resistor. Therefore the current decreases.

再推理：由于 R2 的滑片接在上端节点，真正接入电路的是从滑片到 R2 下端的那一段电阻丝。当滑片向上移动时，滑片到下端的电阻丝长度变长，所以 R2 接入电路的有效电阻增大。在该并联支路两端电压条件下，支路电阻变大，则通过该滑动变阻器支路的电流变小。因此，滑动变阻器中的电流减小。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct circuit-topology route: identify the rheostat connection from the image, translate upward slider motion into increased effective resistance, then apply Ohm’s law. With only one requested method, no additional distinct routes are needed.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as a DC source E feeding a series resistor R1, then a node with a parallel branch containing a fixed vertical resistor and a right-hand sliding resistor R2. On R2, the wiper is connected back to the top node, so the active portion of R2 is the segment between the wiper and the lower terminal; moving the slider upward lengthens this active segment.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to identify the asked change: the slider is moved upward and the required quantity is the current through the sliding resistor.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rheostat rule that resistance is proportional to the length of resistive wire included in the circuit. Moving the wiper upward increases the effective resistance of R2. By Ohm’s law, increasing the resistance of that branch reduces the current through the sliding resistor, even considering the surrounding series-parallel network.
